questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: A student wants to recover pure dry crystals of copper(II) sulphate from an aqueous solution. The correct sequence of steps is
options: heat to concentrate, cool to crystallise, filter, then dry between filter paper
filter, then evaporate to complete dryness in one step
sublime the solution directly
add more water, then filter immediately
questions.explanation: Concentrating by gentle heating, cooling to allow crystals to form, filtering off the crystals, and drying without decomposing them is the standard crystallisation method.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which pair of liquids can be separated using a separating funnel?
options: Water and kerosene
Ethanoic acid and water
Ethanol and water
Water and propanone (acetone)
questions.explanation: A separating funnel works only for immiscible liquids of different densities; water and kerosene do not mix, unlike the other fully miscible pairs listed.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: In paper chromatography, a spot with a low Rf value compared to another spot on the same chromatogram indicates that the substance
options: travelled the farthest distance up the paper
has a lower relative molecular mass
is more volatile than the other substance
is less soluble in the mobile phase or more strongly adsorbed on the paper
questions.explanation: Rf = distance moved by substance / distance moved by solvent; a low Rf means the substance is retained more by the stationary phase (paper), so it moves less.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which technique would best separate crude oil into fractions such as petrol, kerosene, and bitumen for industrial use?
options: Filtration
Simple distillation
Fractional distillation
Decantation
questions.explanation: Crude oil is a mixture of hydrocarbons with a range of boiling points, so a fractionating column separates it into fractions collected at different heights/temperatures.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: A mixture of common salt, sand, and iodine crystals can be separated by first
options: using a magnet to check for iron, then heating to sublime the iodine, then adding water and filtering to separate sand from salt solution
using a separating funnel on the solid mixture
distilling the whole mixture directly
adding water directly and filtering, ignoring the iodine
questions.explanation: A logical stepwise plan removes the sublimable solid (iodine) first by heating, then dissolves the salt in water and filters off the insoluble sand, followed by evaporation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Decantation is most appropriate for separating
options: a mixture of a liquid and an insoluble solid that has settled at the bottom
a dissolved salt from its solution
a mixture of two gases
two miscible liquids of similar density
questions.explanation: Decantation involves carefully pouring off the liquid from a settled solid sediment without disturbing it, useful only when the solid has already settled by gravity.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Why is recrystallisation preferred over simple filtration for purifying a solid organic compound contaminated with a small amount of soluble impurity?
options: It removes insoluble impurities that filtration cannot remove
It changes the chemical identity of the compound to a purer form
It exploits the difference in solubility so that on cooling a saturated solution, only the desired compound crystallises out, leaving impurities in solution
It works only on gaseous mixtures
questions.explanation: Recrystallisation relies on the pure compound and impurity having different solubility behaviour, so the impurity, present in small amount, stays dissolved in the mother liquor while the compound crystallises.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Distilled water used in the laboratory is preferred over tap water for making standard solutions mainly because
options: it is cheaper to produce than tap water
it boils at a lower temperature
it has a higher density than tap water
it is free of dissolved ions and impurities that could interfere with the reaction or titration
questions.explanation: Distillation removes dissolved salts and other non-volatile impurities present in tap water, giving a consistent, ion-free solvent for accurate quantitative work.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: What is the relative molecular mass of Al2(SO4)3? (Al = 27, S = 32, O = 16)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: How many moles of hydrogen atoms are present in 0.2 mole of C2H5OH?
options: 0.6 mole
0.2 mole
2.0 moles
1.2 moles
questions.explanation: Each C2H5OH molecule has 6 hydrogen atoms, so 0.2 mole of C2H5OH contains 0.2 x 6 = 1.2 moles of hydrogen atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: What mass of magnesium (Mg = 24) reacts completely with 200 cm3 of 0.5 mol/dm3 hydrochloric acid, given Mg + 2HCl -> MgCl2 + H2?
questions.explanation: Moles HCl = 0.200 x 0.5 = 0.1 mol. From the equation, 2 mol HCl reacts with 1 mol Mg, so moles Mg = 0.05. Mass = 0.05 x 24 = 1.2 g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: A compound contains 32.4% sodium, 22.5% sulphur, and 45.1% oxygen by mass. What is its empirical formula? (Na = 23, S = 32, O = 16)
options: NaSO2
Na2SO3
Na2SO4
NaSO4

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: What volume of carbon dioxide (at s.t.p.) is produced when 5 g of calcium carbonate reacts completely with excess dilute hydrochloric acid? (Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16; molar volume = 22.4 dm3 at s.t.p.)
questions.explanation: Molar mass CaCO3 = 100. Moles CaCO3 = 5/100 = 0.05. CaCO3 + 2HCl -> CaCl2 + H2O + CO2 (1:1 with CO2), so moles CO2 = 0.05. Volume = 0.05 x 22.4 = 1.12 dm3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Determine the number of moles of ions present in 0.1 mole of Al2(SO4)3 when fully dissociated in solution.
options: 0.5 mole
0.3 mole
0.2 mole
0.1 mole
questions.explanation: Al2(SO4)3 dissociates into 2Al3+ and 3SO4^2-, giving 5 ions per formula unit. 0.1 mole of the compound gives 0.1 x 5 = 0.5 mole of ions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: If 4.6 g of an unknown metal M combines completely with chlorine to form 11.7 g of MCl, what is the relative atomic mass of M? (Cl = 35.5)
questions.explanation: Mass of chlorine combined = 11.7 - 4.6 = 7.1 g, which is 7.1/35.5 = 0.2 mole of Cl, so moles of M = 0.2 (1:1 ratio). Relative atomic mass = 4.6/0.2 = 23.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The Law of Conservation of Mass states that in a chemical reaction
options: the total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products
the volume of reactants equals the volume of products
mass is created but never destroyed
the number of moles of reactants equals the number of moles of products
questions.explanation: This law states that matter is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction, so the total mass before and after the reaction remains constant in a closed system.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: What is the percentage by mass of nitrogen in ammonium sulphate, (NH4)2SO4? (N = 14, H = 1, S = 32, O = 16)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: What is the mass of one mole of water molecules, and how many hydrogen atoms does this mass contain? (H = 1, O = 16)
options: 18 g, containing 1 mole of hydrogen atoms
9 g, containing 1 mole of hydrogen atoms
18 g, containing 2 moles (1.204 x 10^24) of hydrogen atoms
16 g, containing 2 moles of hydrogen atoms
questions.explanation: Molar mass of H2O = (2x1) + 16 = 18 g/mol. Each water molecule has 2 hydrogen atoms, so 1 mole of water contains 2 moles of hydrogen atoms, i.e. 2 x 6.02 x 10^23 = 1.204 x 10^24 atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: A fixed mass of gas occupies 600 cm3 at 20 degC and 1 atmosphere. What volume will it occupy at 1 atmosphere and 100 degC?

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: A gas has a volume of 250 cm3 at a pressure of 1.5 atmospheres. At what pressure will its volume become 375 cm3, assuming constant temperature?
options: 1.0 atmosphere
1.5 atmospheres
0.5 atmosphere
2.25 atmospheres
questions.explanation: By Boyle's Law, P1V1 = P2V2: 1.5 x 250 = P2 x 375, so P2 = 375/375 = 1.0 atmosphere.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of these statements about the kinetic theory applied to liquids is correct?
options: Particles in a liquid vibrate about fixed positions only, with no translational movement
Particles in a liquid have no kinetic energy at room temperature
Particles in a liquid are close together, move about freely, and have moderate forces of attraction between them
Particles in a liquid are far apart with negligible forces of attraction
questions.explanation: Liquid particles are closer than gas particles, can move past one another, and experience intermediate intermolecular forces, unlike the fixed, vibrating particles of a solid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: A gas X diffuses through a porous plug in 40 seconds, while the same volume of oxygen diffuses in 20 seconds under identical conditions. What is the molar mass of gas X? (O2 = 32)
questions.explanation: Rate is inversely proportional to time: rate(X)/rate(O2) = time(O2)/time(X) = 20/40 = 0.5. Graham's Law: rate(X)/rate(O2) = sqrt(M(O2)/M(X)), so 0.5 = sqrt(32/M(X)); squaring: 0.25 = 32/M(X), giving M(X) = 128.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The pressure exerted by a gas on the walls of its container, according to kinetic theory, results directly from
options: the weight of the gas particles settling on the walls
chemical bonding between gas particles and the container
the temperature of the container walls alone
collisions of rapidly moving gas particles against the container walls
questions.explanation: Gas pressure arises from the continuous, random collisions of fast-moving gas particles with the container walls, each collision transferring momentum.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Two gases, methane (CH4, M = 16) and carbon dioxide (CO2, M = 44), are placed on either side of a porous partition. Which gas diffuses faster, and by approximately what factor?
options: Methane, about 2.75 times faster
They diffuse at the same rate
Carbon dioxide, about 1.66 times faster
Methane, about 1.66 times faster
questions.explanation: Rate ratio = sqrt(M(CO2)/M(CH4)) = sqrt(44/16) = sqrt(2.75) = 1.66, so the lighter gas, methane, diffuses about 1.66 times faster than carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: At constant volume, the pressure of a fixed mass of gas is directly proportional to its
options: density only
molar mass
volume
absolute temperature
questions.explanation: This is the Pressure (Gay-Lussac's) Law: at constant volume, P/T = constant, so pressure rises directly with absolute temperature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: A 500 cm3 sample of gas at s.t.p. is heated until its pressure doubles while its volume is kept constant. What is the new temperature in Kelvin?
questions.explanation: At constant volume, P/T = constant: P/273 = 2P/T2, so T2 = 2 x 273 = 546 K.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: A gas occupies 300 cm3 at 27 degC and 750 mmHg pressure. What volume will it occupy at s.t.p. (0 degC, 760 mmHg)?
questions.explanation: Using the combined gas law P1V1/T1 = P2V2/T2 with T1 = 300 K and T2 = 273 K: V2 = (P1 x V1 x T2)/(T1 x P2) = (750 x 300 x 273)/(300 x 760) = 269.4 cm3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: An ion X2- has 18 electrons and a mass number of 32. How many neutrons does the atom of X have?
questions.explanation: X2- has 18 electrons, so the neutral atom X has 18 - 2 = 16 electrons, meaning 16 protons (atomic number 16). Neutrons = mass number - protons = 32 - 16 = 16.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following correctly represents the electronic configuration of the chloride ion, Cl- (atomic number of Cl = 17)?
questions.explanation: Neutral chlorine (17 electrons) has configuration 2,8,7; gaining one electron to form Cl- gives 18 electrons, configuration 2,8,8, isoelectronic with argon.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Down a group in the periodic table, ionisation energy generally
options: decreases only for non-metals, not metals
decreases, because the outermost electron is farther from the nucleus and more shielded
remains constant across all groups
increases, because nuclear charge increases faster than shielding
questions.explanation: Down a group, additional electron shells increase both atomic radius and shielding, so the outer electron is held less tightly and is easier to remove, lowering ionisation energy.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following pairs of species are isoelectronic (have the same number of electrons)?
options: K+ and Ar2+
Na+ and Ne
Na+ and Na
Cl- and Cl
questions.explanation: Na+ has 11 - 1 = 10 electrons, the same as neutral Ne (10 electrons), making them isoelectronic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The shape of the ammonia molecule, NH3, is best described as
options: trigonal planar, with no lone pairs on nitrogen
linear, since nitrogen forms only two bonds
tetrahedral, with four identical bonding pairs
trigonal pyramidal, due to one lone pair on nitrogen repelling the three bonding pairs
questions.explanation: Nitrogen in NH3 has four electron pairs (3 bonding, 1 lone); the lone pair pushes the three N-H bonds together, giving a pyramidal shape rather than a perfect tetrahedron.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which type of crystal structure explains why sodium chloride has a high melting point and conducts electricity only when molten or dissolved?
options: Simple molecular lattice held by weak van der Waals forces
Giant covalent lattice with directional covalent bonds
Giant metallic lattice with delocalised electrons throughout
Giant ionic lattice held by strong electrostatic forces between ions, mobile only when ions are free to move
questions.explanation: NaCl's strong ionic bonds throughout the lattice require large amounts of energy to break (high melting point), and ions can only move freely to carry charge when molten or in solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: An element has electronic configuration 2,8,18,7. To which group of the periodic table does it most likely belong?
options: Group IV
Group VIII (noble gases)
Group II
Group VII (the halogens)
questions.explanation: The outermost shell has 7 electrons, characteristic of Group VII elements (halogens), which readily gain one electron to attain a stable octet.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Van der Waals forces are best described as
options: covalent bonds formed by electron sharing
forces that exist only between ions
weak, temporary attractive forces between molecules arising from fluctuating electron distributions
strong permanent forces due to electron transfer
questions.explanation: Van der Waals forces are weak intermolecular attractions caused by instantaneous dipoles from fluctuating electron clouds, present in all molecules but especially significant in non-polar ones.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Why does diamond have an extremely high melting point compared to iodine, even though both are covalently bonded solids?
options: Diamond conducts electricity while iodine does not, which raises its melting point
Diamond is a giant covalent (macromolecular) structure with strong covalent bonds throughout, while iodine is a simple molecular solid held together only by weak van der Waals forces
Iodine molecules are heavier than diamond's carbon atoms
Diamond contains ionic bonds while iodine contains only covalent bonds
questions.explanation: Diamond requires breaking many strong C-C covalent bonds to melt, whereas melting iodine only requires overcoming weak intermolecular van der Waals forces between I2 molecules, not the covalent bonds within them.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Rust (hydrated iron(III) oxide) forms on iron mainly as a result of the combined action of
options: oxygen and water (moisture) in the air
oxygen alone, with no water required
nitrogen and carbon dioxide
argon and water vapour
questions.explanation: Rusting is an electrochemical process requiring both oxygen and water; iron does not rust in dry air or in oxygen-free water alone.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following is a suitable method for removing both temporary and permanent hardness from water?
options: Ion exchange (using a cation exchange resin)
Simple filtration
Adding more calcium ions
Boiling only
questions.explanation: Ion exchange resins replace Ca2+ and Mg2+ ions with Na+ or H+ ions regardless of which anions are present, so it removes both temporary and permanent hardness, unlike boiling, which only removes temporary hardness.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which gas makes up the smallest percentage by volume among the following components of clean, dry air?
options: Argon
Oxygen
Nitrogen
Carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: Dry air is roughly 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, about 0.93% argon, and only about 0.03-0.04% carbon dioxide, making CO2 the smallest listed component.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Soap forms a scum (curdy precipitate) rather than a lather when used with hard water because
options: hard water contains no dissolved minerals
hard water is more acidic than soft water
the soap reacts with dissolved oxygen in the water
calcium and magnesium ions react with the soap to form an insoluble precipitate
questions.explanation: Soap (a sodium or potassium salt of a fatty acid) reacts with Ca2+/Mg2+ ions in hard water to form an insoluble calcium/magnesium salt (scum), reducing lathering until all these ions are used up.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Photosynthesis in green plants helps regulate the composition of the atmosphere mainly by
options: removing water vapour from the air
removing oxygen from the air and releasing carbon dioxide
removing nitrogen from the air and releasing ammonia
removing carbon dioxide from the air and releasing oxygen
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis uses atmospheric carbon dioxide and water to produce glucose and oxygen, helping to balance the carbon dioxide added by respiration and combustion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following best explains why aquatic life can be harmed by excessive algal growth caused by fertiliser run-off into rivers (eutrophication)?
options: Algae block sunlight needed for water to remain liquid
Algae directly poison fish with toxic gases
Decomposing algae consume dissolved oxygen, depleting it for fish and other aquatic organisms
Algae increase the water's salinity to lethal levels
questions.explanation: Excess nutrients cause algal blooms; when the algae die, their bacterial decomposition consumes large amounts of dissolved oxygen, leading to oxygen depletion that harms or kills aquatic life.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: From a solubility curve, the solubility of potassium nitrate is 32 g per 100 g of water at 20 degC and 110 g per 100 g of water at 60 degC. How much more potassium nitrate can dissolve in 100 g of water when the temperature is raised from 20 degC to 60 degC?
questions.explanation: The additional mass that can dissolve is the difference in solubility: 110 g - 32 g = 78 g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: A solution that contains less dissolved solute than the maximum it could hold at that temperature is described as
options: concentrated only
supersaturated
unsaturated
saturated
questions.explanation: An unsaturated solution can still dissolve more solute at that temperature before reaching the saturation point.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: 100 g of water at 80 degC is saturated with 50 g of a salt. If the solution is cooled to 20 degC, where the solubility is 20 g per 100 g of water, what mass of salt crystallises out?
questions.explanation: The mass that can no longer remain dissolved crystallises out: 50 g - 20 g = 30 g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which factor has the greatest effect on the solubility of a gas in a liquid, other than temperature?
options: Colour of the liquid
Pressure of the gas above the liquid
Density of the container
Shape of the container
questions.explanation: By Henry's Law, the solubility of a gas in a liquid is directly proportional to the partial pressure of that gas above the liquid, at constant temperature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: On a solubility curve graph with temperature on the x-axis and solubility (g per 100 g water) on the y-axis, any point lying above the curve represents a solution that is
options: exactly saturated
unsaturated
supersaturated (unstable, more solute dissolved than the curve predicts)
at its boiling point
questions.explanation: Points above the solubility curve represent solute concentrations exceeding normal saturation at that temperature, characteristic of an unstable supersaturated solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Why does adding common salt to a saturated sugar solution not cause sugar to crystallise out in the same way that cooling would?
options: Salt always increases the solubility of sugar
Salt and sugar have independent solubilities in water and do not directly compete for solubility unless a common-ion or drastic effect is involved
Salt has no effect on any solution
Adding salt raises the boiling point, which always causes crystallisation
questions.explanation: Unlike cooling, which directly lowers a solute's solubility on the curve, adding a different, unrelated solute does not straightforwardly force the first solute to crystallise out.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: A dibasic acid is one that
options: reacts with only two types of bases
can donate two replaceable hydrogen ions per molecule
has a pH of exactly 2
contains two oxygen atoms per molecule
questions.explanation: A dibasic (diprotic) acid, such as H2SO4, has two acidic hydrogen atoms that can be replaced or ionised, unlike a monobasic acid such as HCl.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following salts is likely to give an acidic solution when dissolved in water?
options: Sodium chloride, NaCl
Ammonium chloride, NH4Cl
Sodium carbonate, Na2CO3
Potassium sulphate, K2SO4
questions.explanation: NH4Cl is the salt of a weak base (NH3) and a strong acid (HCl); the NH4+ ion hydrolyses in water to release H+ ions, making the solution acidic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: 30 cm3 of 0.2 mol/dm3 sulphuric acid exactly neutralises 40 cm3 of sodium hydroxide solution. What is the concentration of the NaOH? (H2SO4 + 2NaOH -> Na2SO4 + 2H2O)
options: 0.3 mol/dm3
0.6 mol/dm3
0.2 mol/dm3
0.15 mol/dm3
questions.explanation: Moles H2SO4 = 0.030 x 0.2 = 0.006 mol. Ratio H2SO4:NaOH is 1:2, so moles NaOH = 0.012 mol. Concentration = 0.012/0.040 = 0.3 mol/dm3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following best describes an amphoteric oxide?
options: An oxide that can react with both acids and bases to form a salt and water
An oxide that reacts only with bases
An oxide that does not react with either acids or bases
An oxide that reacts only with acids
questions.explanation: Amphoteric oxides, such as aluminium oxide (Al2O3) and zinc oxide (ZnO), show dual behaviour, reacting with acids as a base and with bases as an acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: What is the pH of a solution with a hydrogen ion concentration of 1 x 10^-3 mol/dm3?

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: A double salt, such as potassium aluminium sulphate (potash alum), is best described as
options: any salt containing two different metals regardless of structure
a salt containing two acidic hydrogen atoms
a salt formed from two different simple salts crystallising together in a fixed ratio, which shows the properties of both constituent ions in solution
a salt with two water molecules of crystallisation only
questions.explanation: Double salts crystallise from a solution containing two simple salts in defined proportions, and in solution they dissociate to give all the constituent ions, e.g., K+, Al3+, and SO4^2- for potash alum.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which observation confirms the presence of a sulphate ion (SO4^2-) in a solution during a qualitative test?
options: A yellow precipitate forms on adding silver nitrate solution
A blue precipitate forms on adding sodium hydroxide
A white precipitate forms on adding dilute hydrochloric acid followed by barium chloride solution, insoluble in excess acid
Effervescence occurs on adding dilute acid
questions.explanation: Barium sulphate is a white precipitate insoluble even in excess dilute hydrochloric acid, distinguishing sulphate from sulphite or carbonate, which would effervesce and dissolve in the acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: A basic salt is one that
options: contains an excess of replaceable acidic hydrogen
always turns litmus red
still contains some hydroxide or oxide ions not fully replaced by an acid
is formed from two different acids
questions.explanation: A basic salt, such as Bi(OH)2Cl, arises when a base is not fully neutralised by the acid, so hydroxide or oxide groups remain in the salt's structure alongside the acid radical.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Titrating 25 cm3 of a 0.1 mol/dm3 NaOH solution with dilute HCl of unknown concentration requires 20 cm3 of the acid to reach the end point. What is the concentration of the HCl?
options: 0.125 mol/dm3
0.1 mol/dm3
0.08 mol/dm3
0.2 mol/dm3
questions.explanation: Moles NaOH = 0.025 x 0.1 = 0.0025 mol = moles HCl (1:1 ratio). Concentration HCl = 0.0025/0.020 = 0.125 mol/dm3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: In the reaction 2FeCl2 + Cl2 -> 2FeCl3, what happens to the oxidation state of iron?
options: It increases from +2 to +3, so iron is oxidised
It increases from +2 to +4
It decreases from +3 to +2, so iron is reduced
It remains unchanged at +2
questions.explanation: Fe2+ loses an electron to become Fe3+ (oxidation state rises from +2 to +3), meaning iron is oxidised while chlorine is reduced from 0 to -1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: What is the oxidation number of nitrogen in the nitrate ion, NO3-?
questions.explanation: Let N = x: x + 3(-2) = -1, so x - 6 = -1, giving x = +5.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which half-equation correctly represents the reduction of manganate(VII) ions in acidic solution?
options: MnO4- -> Mn2+ + 5e-
MnO4- + 5e- -> Mn2+
questions.explanation: This balanced half-equation shows manganese going from +7 in MnO4- to +2 in Mn2+, gaining 5 electrons, with the oxygens balanced by H+ and H2O in acidic conditions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following describes a disproportionation reaction?
options: An acid neutralises a base completely
Two different elements are both oxidised
A single species is simultaneously oxidised and reduced in the same reaction
A precipitate forms from two soluble salts
questions.explanation: In disproportionation, one species acts as both the oxidising and reducing agent, being simultaneously oxidised and reduced, as when chlorine reacts with cold dilute sodium hydroxide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: In the reaction between zinc metal and dilute sulphuric acid, Zn + H2SO4 -> ZnSO4 + H2, which species is reduced?
options: H+ ions, to form hydrogen gas
Zn atoms, to form Zn2+
SO4^2- ions
H2 gas, to form H+ ions
questions.explanation: H+ ions gain electrons (from the oxidation of zinc) to form neutral H2 gas, so hydrogen is reduced, while zinc is oxidised to Zn2+.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following metals would most readily displace copper from copper(II) sulphate solution, based on the reactivity (electrochemical) series?
options: Magnesium
Gold
Silver
Platinum
questions.explanation: Magnesium is more reactive (more easily oxidised) than copper, so it readily displaces copper from solution; silver, gold, and platinum are all less reactive than copper.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: What is the change in oxidation number of carbon when methane (CH4) is completely combusted to carbon dioxide (CO2)?
options: It increases from -4 to +4, an oxidation of 8 units
It decreases from -4 to +4
It remains unchanged
It increases from -2 to +2
questions.explanation: In CH4, carbon is -4 (each H is +1). In CO2, carbon is +4 (each O is -2). The oxidation number rises by 8, confirming combustion is an oxidation process for carbon.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: A reducing agent in a redox reaction is the species that
options: always contains oxygen
is itself reduced while causing another species to be oxidised
remains unchanged throughout the reaction
is itself oxidised while causing another species to be reduced
questions.explanation: The reducing agent donates electrons to another species (reducing it) and, in doing so, is itself oxidised.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: During the electrolysis of concentrated brine (sodium chloride solution) using inert electrodes, the products formed are
options: chlorine at the cathode and hydrogen at the anode
chlorine gas at the anode, hydrogen gas at the cathode, and sodium hydroxide left in solution
sodium metal at the cathode and oxygen at the anode
only water is produced at both electrodes
questions.explanation: In concentrated brine, Cl- ions are preferentially discharged at the anode (chlorine gas) and H+ from water is discharged at the cathode (hydrogen gas), leaving Na+ and OH- ions, i.e. NaOH, in solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: What quantity of electric charge, in coulombs, is required to deposit 1 mole of silver from silver nitrate solution, given Ag+ + e- -> Ag?
options: 1 C
questions.explanation: Depositing 1 mole of silver requires 1 mole of electrons, which is exactly 1 Faraday, equal to 96,500 coulombs.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: A current of 5 amperes is passed through molten lead(II) bromide for 3860 seconds. What mass of lead is deposited at the cathode? (Pb = 207, 1 Faraday = 96500 C, Pb2+ + 2e- -> Pb)
questions.explanation: Charge = It = 5 x 3860 = 19300 C. Moles electrons = 19300/96500 = 0.2. Moles Pb = 0.2/2 = 0.1. Mass = 0.1 x 207 = 20.7 g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following factors does NOT influence which ion is preferentially discharged at an electrode during electrolysis of a mixed electrolyte?
options: The concentration of the ion in solution
The colour of the electrolyte solution
The nature of the electrode (inert or reactive)
The relative position of the ion in the electrochemical (reactivity) series
questions.explanation: Preferential discharge depends on the ion's position in the electrochemical series, its concentration, and the electrode material, but the colour of the solution has no bearing on which ion is discharged.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: In the electrolytic refining (purification) of copper, the impure copper is made the
options: salt bridge connecting both half-cells
anode, so that it dissolves and pure copper is deposited at the cathode
electrolyte itself, rather than an electrode
cathode, so that pure copper dissolves off it
questions.explanation: In copper refining, impure copper is the anode (dissolves as Cu2+ ions), a strip of pure copper is the cathode (Cu2+ is deposited), and impurities either dissolve or fall as anode sludge.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following correctly states the order of preferential discharge for cations at the cathode during electrolysis (most easily discharged first)?
options: Only hydrogen ions can ever be discharged at the cathode
Ions of more reactive metals are always discharged first, regardless of position in the series
Ions of less reactive metals are discharged before ions of more reactive metals
All cations are discharged at exactly the same rate
questions.explanation: Less reactive metal ions (lower in the electrochemical series, e.g., Cu2+, Ag+) are more easily reduced (discharged) at the cathode than more reactive metal ions such as Na+ or K+, which tend to remain in solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: During the electrolysis of dilute sulphuric acid, the volume ratio of gas collected at the cathode to gas collected at the anode is approximately
options: 2:1 (hydrogen to oxygen)
1:2 (hydrogen to oxygen)
questions.explanation: Water is electrolysed to give hydrogen at the cathode and oxygen at the anode in the same mole ratio as in H2O (2H2 : O2), so twice the volume of hydrogen is produced compared to oxygen.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: When ammonium nitrate dissolves in water, the temperature of the solution drops noticeably. This process is best classified as
options: endothermic, since heat is absorbed from the surroundings
exothermic, since heat is released to the surroundings
isothermic, since no heat is exchanged
a physical change with no energy change at all
questions.explanation: The temperature drop shows that the dissolution process absorbs heat energy from its surroundings (the water), making it endothermic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: For the reversible reaction 2SO2(g) + O2(g) <=> 2SO3(g), which condition would shift the equilibrium towards the formation of more sulphur trioxide, based on Le Chatelier's Principle applied to concentration?
options: Adding a catalyst
Increasing the concentration of oxygen
Adding an inert gas at constant volume
Removing sulphur dioxide from the mixture
questions.explanation: Increasing the concentration of a reactant (oxygen) shifts the equilibrium to the right (towards products) to partially consume the added reactant, forming more SO3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: A catalyst added to a reversible reaction at equilibrium will
options: speed up both the forward and reverse reactions equally, so equilibrium is reached faster without shifting its position
shift the equilibrium position towards the reactants only
shift the equilibrium position towards the products only
have no effect on the rate of either the forward or reverse reaction
questions.explanation: A catalyst lowers the activation energy of both forward and reverse reactions equally, so the same equilibrium position is reached more quickly, without changing the equilibrium concentrations.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: In an energy profile diagram for an exothermic reaction, which of the following is true?
options: The reactants and products have identical energy levels
The products have higher energy than the reactants
The activation energy is always zero
The products have lower energy than the reactants, and energy is released overall
questions.explanation: In an exothermic reaction, the products end up at a lower energy level than the reactants, with the difference released as heat to the surroundings.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Doubling the concentration of a reactant in a reaction typically increases the rate of reaction mainly because
options: there are more reactant particles per unit volume, increasing the frequency of effective collisions
the reactant particles move faster on average
the activation energy of the reaction is lowered
the temperature of the system automatically rises
questions.explanation: A higher concentration means more particles are packed into the same volume, increasing the collision frequency between reacting particles and thus the reaction rate, without changing individual particle speed.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following would NOT shift the position of equilibrium in a reversible gaseous reaction?
options: Changing the concentration of a reactant or product
Adding a catalyst
Changing the temperature
Changing the pressure (for reactions with unequal gas moles)
questions.explanation: A catalyst only affects the rate at which equilibrium is reached; it does not alter the equilibrium position, unlike changes in temperature, pressure, or concentration.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The enthalpy change for a reaction is defined as
options: the activation energy required to start the reaction
the total kinetic energy of all reacting particles
the rate at which reactants are converted to products
the heat energy absorbed or released during the reaction at constant pressure
questions.explanation: Enthalpy change (delta H) measures the heat exchanged with the surroundings during a chemical reaction carried out at constant pressure; negative for exothermic, positive for endothermic reactions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Why does powdered calcium carbonate react faster with dilute hydrochloric acid than an equal mass of large calcium carbonate lumps?
options: Powdered calcium carbonate is a different chemical compound from the lumps
The acid is more concentrated when reacting with powder
Powder has a lower activation energy requirement than lumps of the same substance
Powdered calcium carbonate has a much greater surface area exposed to the acid, increasing the frequency of collisions
questions.explanation: Breaking a solid into smaller particles greatly increases its total surface area in contact with the acid, allowing more frequent collisions between acid particles and the solid, speeding up the reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: What is the molecular formula of the alkane containing 6 carbon atoms?
options: C6H12
C6H6
C6H10
C6H14
questions.explanation: Alkanes follow the general formula CnH2n+2; for n = 6, this gives C6H14 (hexane).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following pairs of compounds are structural isomers of each other?
options: Butane (C4H10) and 2-methylpropane (C4H10)
Methane (CH4) and methanol (CH3OH)
Ethane (C2H6) and ethene (C2H4)
Propane (C3H8) and propanol (C3H7OH)
questions.explanation: Isomers share the same molecular formula but differ in structural arrangement; butane and 2-methylpropane both have the formula C4H10 but different carbon skeletons (straight chain vs branched).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Ethanol can be produced industrially on a small/traditional scale by which biological process, using yeast enzymes acting on sugar?
options: Cracking
Fermentation
Polymerisation
Hydrolysis
questions.explanation: Fermentation uses yeast enzymes (zymase) to convert glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide under anaerobic conditions, a traditional method of producing ethanol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: What type of reaction occurs when ethene (C2H4) reacts with hydrogen gas in the presence of a nickel catalyst to form ethane (C2H6)?
options: Substitution reaction
Condensation reaction
Addition (hydrogenation) reaction
Elimination reaction
questions.explanation: Hydrogen adds directly across the C=C double bond of ethene with a nickel catalyst, converting the unsaturated alkene into the saturated alkane ethane; this is an addition reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Cracking of long-chain hydrocarbons from crude oil fractions is carried out mainly to
options: increase the average molecular mass of the hydrocarbons
break large, less useful alkane molecules into smaller, more useful alkanes and alkenes
convert alkenes into alkanes only
remove sulphur impurities from the hydrocarbons
questions.explanation: Cracking uses heat and/or a catalyst to break long hydrocarbon chains into shorter, more commercially useful alkanes and alkenes, such as petrol components and ethene for the plastics industry.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which functional group is present in an aldehyde, distinguishing it from a ketone?
options: C=O located strictly between two carbon chains with no hydrogen attached
-CHO, with the carbonyl carbon bonded to at least one hydrogen atom
-COOH
-OH
questions.explanation: Aldehydes have the carbonyl group at the end of the carbon chain, bonded to a hydrogen atom (-CHO); ketones have the carbonyl group between two carbon atoms with no hydrogen directly attached.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Ethanoic acid (CH3COOH) reacts with sodium carbonate to produce
options: ethanol and sodium carbonate remains unreacted
only carbon dioxide gas, with no salt formed
sodium ethanoate, water, and carbon dioxide gas
sodium ethanoate and hydrogen gas only
questions.explanation: As a carboxylic acid, ethanoic acid reacts with carbonates just like other acids: 2CH3COOH + Na2CO3 -> 2CH3COONa + H2O + CO2, producing effervescence.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following best distinguishes a saturated hydrocarbon from an unsaturated one using bromine water?
options: A saturated hydrocarbon decolourises bromine water while an unsaturated one does not
Neither type of hydrocarbon reacts with bromine water under any condition
An unsaturated hydrocarbon decolourises bromine water rapidly, while a saturated one does not readily react
Both saturated and unsaturated hydrocarbons decolourise bromine water at the same rate
questions.explanation: Unsaturated hydrocarbons (alkenes/alkynes) undergo addition reactions with bromine, quickly decolourising bromine water, while saturated alkanes react only slowly, if at all, under normal conditions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which polymer is formed by the condensation polymerisation of a diol and a dicarboxylic acid, with the loss of water molecules?
options: Polystyrene
Polyvinyl chloride (PVC)
Polyester
Polythene (polyethene)
questions.explanation: Polyesters, such as Terylene, are formed by condensation polymerisation between a diol and a dicarboxylic acid, releasing water molecules as the ester linkages form, unlike addition polymers like polythene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Natural rubber is an example of a naturally occurring polymer whose monomer unit is
options: glucose
isoprene (2-methylbuta-1,3-diene)
amino acids
ethene
questions.explanation: Natural rubber is a polymer of isoprene units joined together, giving it its characteristic elasticity, distinct from synthetic addition polymers derived from ethene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which method of extraction is most suitable for a highly reactive metal such as sodium, which cannot be reduced by carbon?
options: Reduction with carbon monoxide in a blast furnace
Heating the ore alone in air
Displacement using a less reactive metal
Electrolysis of the molten chloride
questions.explanation: Highly reactive metals like sodium form very stable compounds that carbon cannot reduce, so electrolysis of the molten ore/salt is used instead, as in the Downs process for sodium.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which property distinguishes non-metals from metals in terms of their oxides' behaviour with water?
options: Only metal oxides ever dissolve in water
Non-metal oxides tend to be basic, while metal oxides tend to be acidic
Non-metal oxides tend to be acidic, while metal oxides tend to be basic
Both metal and non-metal oxides are always neutral in water
questions.explanation: Non-metal oxides, such as SO2 and CO2, generally dissolve in water to form acids, while metal oxides, such as Na2O and CaO, generally form alkaline solutions (bases).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The rusting of iron can be prevented by galvanising, which involves
options: coating the iron with a layer of zinc, which is more reactive and corrodes preferentially, protecting the iron
painting the iron with an oxide-based paint only
coating the iron with a layer of copper, which is less reactive
heating the iron strongly to remove all moisture permanently
questions.explanation: Galvanising coats iron with zinc; even if the coating is scratched, zinc, being more reactive, corrodes sacrificially before the iron, providing ongoing (cathodic) protection.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following correctly ranks three metals from most reactive to least reactive, based on the reactivity series: potassium, iron, gold?
options: Potassium > Iron > Gold
Gold > Potassium > Iron
Gold > Iron > Potassium
Iron > Potassium > Gold
questions.explanation: In the standard reactivity series, potassium is among the most reactive metals, iron is moderately reactive, and gold is one of the least reactive (unreactive) metals.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Sulphur dioxide gas is manufactured into sulphuric acid via the Contact Process, in which SO2 is first catalytically oxidised to SO3 using which catalyst?
options: Iron catalyst with a promoter
Nickel catalyst
Platinum gauze only
Vanadium(V) oxide, V2O5
questions.explanation: The Contact Process uses vanadium(V) oxide (V2O5) as the catalyst to oxidise sulphur dioxide to sulphur trioxide, which is then converted to sulphuric acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following non-metals is used in water treatment as a disinfectant, while also being a highly reactive halogen capable of displacing bromine and iodine from their salt solutions?
options: Carbon
Argon
Nitrogen
Chlorine
questions.explanation: Chlorine is a reactive halogen used to disinfect water and, being more reactive than bromine and iodine, can displace them from their respective halide solutions in a displacement reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Why is mild steel (an alloy of iron with a small amount of carbon), rather than pure iron, generally used for construction purposes?
options: Mild steel does not conduct electricity, unlike pure iron
Pure iron is more resistant to corrosion than mild steel
The added carbon disrupts the regular metallic lattice, making the alloy stronger and harder than pure iron
Mild steel is far less dense than pure iron
questions.explanation: Alloying introduces atoms of a different size into the metal lattice, disrupting the orderly layers of metal ions and preventing them from sliding easily, which increases hardness and strength compared to the pure metal.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which gas is produced when a reactive metal such as zinc reacts with a dilute acid, and how would you test for it?
options: Oxygen gas, tested with a glowing splint which relights
Chlorine gas, tested with damp litmus paper which bleaches
Hydrogen gas, tested with a lit splint which produces a 'pop' sound
Carbon dioxide gas, tested with limewater which turns milky
questions.explanation: Reactive metals react with dilute acids to liberate hydrogen gas, which gives the characteristic 'pop' sound when a lit splint is placed at the mouth of the test tube.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: What is the molar mass of water, H2O? (H = 1, O = 16)
options: 20 g/mol
17 g/mol
18 g/mol
16 g/mol
questions.explanation: Molar mass of H2O = (2 x 1) + 16 = 18 g/mol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following best describes an exothermic reaction?
options: A reaction that only occurs at very low temperatures
A reaction that absorbs heat energy from the surroundings
A reaction that produces no energy change
A reaction that releases heat energy to the surroundings
questions.explanation: An exothermic reaction releases heat to the surroundings, often causing a rise in temperature that can be felt or measured.
